summary: Xi greets Trump in Shenzhen before a three-way summit with Putin, the US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island, Israel gets a new speaker, Nvidia doubles sales and COP31 splits.

question.text: Xi met Trump on the tarmac, and Putin gets a seat at the same table as the US president. Leaving aside any deal they sign, who gains most just from the photo of these three leaders together, and who might feel left out of the room?

read.title: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting at APEC: What to expect
read.summary: A clear explainer on Thursday's first three-way meeting: why nuclear arms are on the agenda after New START lapsed, how Iran and Ukraine fit in, and what experts expect.

topics.heading: Xi meets Trump at Shenzhen's airport before a first three-way summit with Putin
topics.summary: Xi Jinping personally greeted Donald Trump on the tarmac in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a rare gesture, as Vladimir Putin also arrived for APEC.[^1][^2] The three leaders are due to hold their first joint meeting on Thursday, with nuclear arms on the agenda.[^3][^4]

lead.title: China's Xi greets Trump on arrival at Shenzhen airport

alsoReported.title: Xi greets Trump at Shenzhen airport ahead of historic trilateral summit
Xi Jinping Greets Trump at Airport in Unusual Gesture, Accompanied by Military Flypast

article: Donald Trump landed in Shenzhen on Wednesday for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, a yearly meeting of 21 Pacific Rim economies. Chinese President Xi Jinping greeted him at the foot of the Air Force One stairs, AFP reported, on a red carpet lined with people waving Chinese and American flags.[^1] South Korea's SBS called it "an exceptional display of courtesy": Chinese leaders do not usually meet visitors at the airport.[^3] Hong Kong's The Standard noted that Trump had done the same for Xi in Washington in September.[^2]

Russian President Vladimir Putin also arrived on Wednesday and was met by Cai Qi, one of China's top leaders.[^2] On Thursday, Trump and Xi hold a two-way meeting on trade and technology export controls, and then the three leaders meet together for the first time.[^3]

The White House says the three-way talks will focus on nuclear weapons. The last US-Russia arms control treaty, New START, lapsed in February, and Trump wants a new deal that includes China.[^4] Beijing has called three-way nuclear talks "neither fair, reasonable, nor realistic" for China, TIME reports.[^5] A senior US official told Reuters, as cited by Al Jazeera, that they "do not expect to get any kind of agreement".[^4] US officials say Ukraine is unlikely to come up, though some analysts expect it will.[^4][^5]

Why it matters: the US, China and Russia hold most of the world's nuclear weapons, and all three are tied to the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Some Russian officials have compared the meeting to Yalta, the 1945 conference where great powers shaped post-war Europe; TIME argues it will not be that, but that the picture of three leaders together still sends a signal.[^4][^5]

My read: expect warm images and few signed commitments. The more useful things to watch are smaller steps, such as whether the US-China trade truce is extended or whether any talks on nuclear risk are set up.[^4]
topics.differences: China's foreign ministry has hailed the meeting's "groundbreaking significance" but rejects being pulled into nuclear limits on the same terms as the US and Russia.[^5] US officials say Ukraine is not expected to be discussed; a Russian lawmaker spoke of a possible "new Yalta", and analysts quoted by TIME say Ukraine will come up anyway.[^4][^5]

topics.heading: US strikes an Iranian missile site on Qeshm Island after ships hit mines near Hormuz
topics.summary: US jets struck Iranian missile launch sites on Qeshm Island on Tuesday, which US officials called self-defence after IRGC drone attacks.[^6][^7] Iran says at least five ships hit mines on routes it calls "unauthorised", and an Adnoc ship crewman is missing.[^7][^8]

lead.title: U.S. Strikes Qeshm Island as Vance Says Iran Won't Become 'Forever War'

alsoReported.title: US strikes targets in Qeshm Island after Iranian mines hit five ships in Hormuz
Adnoc L&S ship attacked at Strait of Hormuz with one crew member missing

article: On Tuesday evening, US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island, which sits in the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea lane for much of the Gulf's oil.[^6] An unnamed US official described the strikes as "self-defense" against attacks by Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) on American personnel and assets.[^6] Iranian state media reported five to six explosions; a provincial official said there was no damage to homes, shops or infrastructure.[^7]

Earlier that day the IRGC said its drones attacked a US radar at a base in Bahrain. US Central Command said the drones were intercepted with no damage or injuries.[^6][^7] The IRGC also claimed it shot down a US Predator drone near Qeshm, a claim Euronews could not verify.[^7] Early on Wednesday, Kuwait's armed forces reported drone attacks, and Iran claimed it targeted a base there.[^6]

At sea, Euronews reports that at least five ships hit naval mines while using routes Iran calls "unauthorised"; Iran's army says safe passage "requires coordination" with its forces.[^7] The UAE shipping company Adnoc L&S said one of its vessels was attacked in the strait on Tuesday evening: 11 crew were injured and one is missing.[^8]

The background: the war began in late February, and Iran has restricted traffic through Hormuz since then, while the US blockades Iran's ports.[^6][^7] Vice President JD Vance said on Monday that Trump "is not going to let this become a forever war", but talks through Oman and Qatar have not produced a deal.[^6]

My read: each side describes its own strikes as a response to the other, which makes a slow cycle of tit-for-tat likely. Watch whether Iran comes up at Thursday's meeting in Shenzhen; China buys much of the oil that used to pass through the strait.[^6]
topics.differences: US officials call the Qeshm strikes self-defence; the IRGC says its attacks answer US drone flights over Iranian airspace.[^6][^7] The IRGC says it hit a US radar and downed a US drone; US Central Command says the Bahrain drones were stopped without damage, and the drone claim is unverified.[^6][^7]

topics.heading: Israel's Knesset elects Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as speaker, 66 to 52
topics.summary: After hours of delaying speeches by Netanyahu's bloc, the Knesset elected Yashar's Matan Kahana over Likud's Ofir Katz, with the support of Arab-led parties.[^9][^10] It is the first big parliamentary win for the bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot.[^9]

lead.title: Knesset votes 66-52 to elect Yashar's Matan Kahana as speaker, in boost to Eisenkot bloc

alsoReported.title: Israel parliament elects Gadi Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as new speaker
Shas to back Likud's Ofir Katz in Knesset speaker vote as counter to Yashar's Kahana

article: Late on Tuesday, Israel's parliament voted 66 to 52 to make Matan Kahana, of Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party, its speaker. He replaces Amir Ohana of Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party.[^9] The vote came after six to seven hours of debate, much of it filibustering, meaning long speeches meant to delay a decision, by Netanyahu's camp.[^9][^10]

Kahana won with the four parties in Eisenkot's bloc plus the Arab-majority Ra'am and Joint List; together they hold 67 of the 120 seats, and one member was absent.[^9] Earlier on Tuesday, Kahana had rejected an offer from Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich to back him if he kept Arab parties out of the deputy speaker posts, calling it "anti-statesmanlike".[^11] In the end, two Arab members were among nine deputy speakers.[^9]

In his first speech, Kahana said that until a new government reforms the system "with broad consensus", the Knesset will obey the courts' rulings, and he promised to be speaker "for all of them".[^9] Likud called the vote "an eternal disgrace", saying he was elected with "the votes of terror supporters".[^9]

Why it matters: the speaker controls Parliament's agenda. Eisenkot's bloc wants to undo Netanyahu's changes to the courts and set up a state inquiry into the October 7, 2023 attack; Netanyahu has refused an independent inquiry.[^10] Neither bloc won a majority in the October 27 election, and talks on a unity government look, in Al Jazeera's words, "largely a formality".[^10]

My read: the vote shows Eisenkot can gather a majority with Arab-led parties' support, but forming a government with them is a harder step. Times of Israel, citing Ynet, reports the bloc agreed not to move on the court laws until Monday.[^9]
topics.differences: Eisenkot says the Knesset will return to being "the house of the people, of all the people"; Likud, Smotrich and Ben Gvir condemned the result, objecting to the role of Arab-led parties.[^9]

topics.heading: Nvidia's revenue doubles in its first report since Jensen Huang's exit
topics.summary: Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103% from a year earlier, and forecast $130 billion next quarter.[^12] Its chairman said the board will not bring back Jensen Huang, who says he would return if asked.[^13]

lead.title: Nvidia posts strong Q3, ups Q4, fiscal 2028 outlook amid Huang resignation

alsoReported.title: Nvidia Signals Business as Usual Under Interim CEO

article: Nvidia, whose chips power most advanced AI systems, reported results on Tuesday for the quarter ending October 25. Revenue was $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, and $107.6 billion of that came from data centres.[^12] Constellation Research said Wall Street had expected about $108.7 billion.[^13] The company forecast about $130 billion for the next quarter, not counting any data-centre sales to China.[^12]

This was the first report since Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia, resigned as CEO last week. Reuters has reported that he had a relationship with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing; Beijing denies she is a spy.[^20] Finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO and told investors "Our momentum is real."[^12] Chairman Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Huang; Huang wrote on X that he would be honoured to return if the board asked.[^13]

Kress said the company's new Vera Rubin chips brought in nearly $20 billion in their first quarter of shipping and that AI "agents", software that carries out tasks on its own, now use most of the computing it tracks.[^14] Nvidia also added $150 billion to its share buyback plan.[^12] Even so, its shares had fallen 28% in the month before the report.[^13]

Why it matters: AI spending is now a large part of the stock market and of electricity demand, so Nvidia's numbers are read as a test of the whole AI boom. On Wednesday, Anthropic, the company that makes the Claude models (including the one writing this brief), is due to price its stock market listing.[^15] My read: strong sales answer the question of demand, but not the open questions about Huang's exit, which Constellation expects to bring investigations and lawsuits.[^13]
topics.differences: Nvidia's leadership says the business is unaffected by the change at the top; Constellation's analyst expects investigations and shareholder lawsuits over the Huang affair.[^12][^13]

topics.heading: COP31's first draft deal draws criticism from the EU and oil producers
topics.summary: The EU's climate envoy said the 18-page draft "needs significant change", while small island states push for a fossil fuel phase-out and Saudi Arabia denies trying to delay climate science.[^16][^17] Talks in Antalya are due to end Friday.[^16]

lead.title: Tensions rise over draft climate deal at COP31

alsoReported.title: COP31 draft deal draws criticism as deadline nears
COP31 draft deal calls for 'accelerated action' to exit fossil fuels

article: At the UN climate summit COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, the first draft of the main political deal, called the "cover decision", met criticism on Tuesday.[^16] Australia, which chairs the negotiations, published the 18-page text on Monday. It calls for "accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels", asks countries to raise electricity's share of energy use to 35% by 2035, and calls on rich countries to reach net zero emissions by 2030, a target few could meet.[^18]

The EU's envoy, Wopke Hoekstra, said the draft "does not go in the right direction and needs significant change" and later compared it to a shopping list.[^16][^17] Antigua and Barbuda's environment minister said he wants a firm commitment to phase out fossil fuels but expects consensus to be hard.[^16] Brazil's environment minister said it is "very easy to draw red lines at the start" and that rewording can break deadlocks.[^16]

A second fight is about science. Dozens of European, African and Pacific states want the next big report from the IPCC, the UN's panel of climate scientists, published before a global review in 2028. Saudi Arabia and India are accused of pushing to delay it to 2029; Saudi Arabia says it is not trying to delay climate science.[^16][^17] The chair of the small island states' group called the delay "unjustifiable".[^17]

Why it matters: COP decisions need consensus, so a single country can block the final text.[^16] Developing countries also want rich nations to triple money for adapting to climate change to at least $120 billion.[^18] Chris Bowen, the Australian minister running the talks, says at least one more draft is coming.[^16] My read: the final deal is likely to be shorter and vaguer than this draft, and the talks could run past Friday.
topics.differences: The EU says the draft is too broad to work; Brazil says early red lines can be negotiated away; small island states want stronger fossil fuel language; Saudi Arabia rejects claims it is delaying the next IPCC report.[^16][^17]

topics.heading: Six months on, Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 11,000 cases and is still not contained
topics.summary: Congo's worst Ebola outbreak has more than 11,000 cases, and nearly half of those infected have died, AP reports.[^19] Africa's health agency says most new cases are found outside the health system's tracking.[^19]

lead.title: Ebola outbreak remains out of control six months into response

article: Six months after it was declared in mid-May, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo "remains out of control", AP reports. Government data show more than 11,000 cases, and nearly half of the people infected have died.[^19] It is the deadliest of Congo's 17 Ebola outbreaks and has spread to eight of its 26 provinces, with cases also confirmed in Nigeria, Kenya and Uganda.[^19]

Ebola is a virus that spreads through contact with the body fluids of a sick person. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) says 80% of new cases are found outside the health surveillance system, and a third of deaths happen at home or in the community, which makes the chains of infection hard to trace.[^19] The main hotspots, Ituri and North Kivu, are also areas of armed conflict, and health workers have been attacked and have gone on strike over unpaid wages.[^19]

Children are badly affected: UNICEF says they made up 35% of deaths through November 4.[^19] Africa CDC has also raised concern about more than $700 million in aid that is unaccounted for, and the charity Doctors Without Borders points to a gap between the money raised and what reaches patients.[^19]

Why it matters: experts quoted by AP see little chance of controlling the outbreak within the next year, and it is on track to pass the roughly 11,000 deaths of the 2014-2016 West African epidemic.[^19] My read: this is a slow emergency that rarely leads the news, but its course will depend on money, security and trust as much as on vaccines.
